name: Torque
description: Torque is the street name of a mid-the Gray Zone aug-body artist whose neural feed, Raw Chrome, documents extreme voluntary augmentation procedures performed outside licensed clinics — back-alley chop shops, unlicensed rippers, and experimental self-modification. Their own body is a working portfolio: a fully replaced left arm in exposed brushed-titanium lattice, a secondary jaw hinge that opens 180 degrees, and sub-dermal LED threading that pulses in sync with their heartbeat. Raw Chrome distinguishes itself from corporate aug-content by showing the pain, the infection risk, the recovery, and the class politics of who can afford safe augmentation and who cannot.
cultural_impact: Raw Chrome has shifted the public conversation around aug accessibility — several underground clinics now voluntarily follow safety protocols Torque developed and broadcasts as open-source guides. The feed is banned on three major corporate platforms but thrives on decentralized mesh-net nodes.
locations: Underbelly Clinic Row, the Gray Zone Ward 3
The Solder & Skin Market, Milwaukee South Corridor
story_hooks: A Tier 4 aug-corporation offers to sponsor Torque, which would fund a legitimate clinic in the Gray Zone — but the contract includes a clause that would give the corp ownership of all documented procedures as IP.
One of the back-alley surgeons Torque filmed has gone missing, and the last procedure documented on Raw Chrome appears to have installed something in the patient that no one recognizes.
Torque's feed captures footage of military-grade chrome being sold illegally at a the Gray Zone ripper — the kind that should only exist in Tier 5 corporate security forces.
platform: Raw Chrome (decentralized mesh-net feed, haptic surgery overlay)
follower_count: ~1.4 million across mesh nodes, heavily Tier 1-3
controversy: In 2209, Torque broadcast a live procedure where a the Gray Zone resident received a black-market military neural interface; the feed was cut by a corporate interdiction signal mid-surgery, and Torque spent six days in a Meridian Security holding facility before community pressure secured their release. The patient's identity was never confirmed.
